question: Which claims and dependencies sit behind a digital cash leg?
answer: Bank deposits, central-bank money and reserve-backed coins create different claims. The selected component records show who owes money and which reserve, distribution or settlement arrangement the route depends on; a shared ledger alone does not settle every claim.

items.title: Cash legs & tokenized bank money
kv: Compare stablecoins, commercial-bank deposit tokens, central-bank-backed settlement units and orchestration layers without treating them as interchangeable cash.
Issuer liability, representation, orchestration and legal discharge remain separate.

Identify the money issuer: central bank, commercial bank or stablecoin issuer. · Identify the legal claim: reserve, deposit, redemption right or payment-system balance. · Identify its representation: conventional account, private ledger or public-chain token. · Identify eligible access: customer, vetted wallet, participant or settlement bank. · Identify the orchestration layer: application, Swift, Partior or smart contract. · Locate final settlement or redemption on bank books, RTGS, reserve pool or same ledger. · Preserve correction, insolvency, downtime and operating-clock boundaries.
